A 68-year-old woman arrives at the emergency department with sudden-onset weakness. She was
eating dinner with her family an hour ago when she began slurring her speech and experiencing
weakness in her right arm. She attempted to stand but fell to her right side without hitting her head or
losing consciousness. Her medical history includes hypertension managed with amlodipine, and she
has a 45-pack-year smoking history. On examination, her temperature is 99.6°F (37.6°C), blood
pressure is 151/93 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 18/min. Neurological findings include
right-sided facial weakness sparing the forehead and 2/5 strength in the right wrist, elbow, and knee,
while strength on the left side is 5/5. Fingerstick blood glucose is 106 mg/dL. A non-contrast CT scan of
the head shows no hyperdense lesions. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
Answer Choices: (A) CT angiogram of the head and neck (B) Immediate blood pressure reduction (C)
MRI of the head (D) Aspirin administration (E) Antiplatelet therapy (F) Aspirin and atorvastatin (G)
Neurosurgical consultation (H) Heparin infusion (I) Observation and serial neurological exams (J)
Alteplase
 A. Observation and serial neurological exams
B. Alteplase
C. Neurosurgical consultation
D. Immediate blood pressure reduction
